sample_unit: clinicians (resident emergency medicine physicians and advanced practice providers)

links.outcome: Whether structured clinician interviews during early implementation identify workflow-fit and use factors for a CDS tool
links.effect: 10-minute academic detailing interviews (n=16) identified five categories of factors affecting CDS use (design, understanding, busy ED, patient perception, opaque referral process) and allowed concurrent correction of misconceptions.
links.quote: Thus, academic detailing can inform both real-time adjustments of a tool's implementation, for example, refinement of the language used to introduce the tool, and larger scale redesign of the CDS tool to better fit the dynamic work environment of clinicians.

unlisted_practices: Academic detailing (brief personal visits by a tool expert) to educate clinicians and gather implementation feedback on a deployed CDS tool

screen.practice: academic detailing (clinician education and feedback interviews)
screen.reason: Empirical qualitative study evaluating academic detailing (clinician education visits) to support the real-world deployment and clinician use of a machine learning-based emergency department fall risk CDS tool.
